paragraphs.text: "No rest. No mercy. No matter what."
Akroma asked for only one thing from her troops: unwavering, unconditional loyalty.
Redeemers rise with the sun, and the spirits of the people rise with them.
"We all borrowed life from the Ancestor to exist in this world. Today, I repay that debt."
"It's easy to lose sight of hope until you gaze out from my vantage point."
The slivers would survive, even at the expense of every other creature on Otaria.
"It is not yet time."
"I feed my hatred to the righteous and they join my crusade." —Akroma, angelic avenger
"Every moment has its own savior."
Overcoming extinction has only made the slivers more determined to live.
The Mirari glows in her eyes.
His outer calm belies his inner fury.
"What cage would you rather be inside of than out?" —Daru riddle
The first wave of slivers perished from the Riptide wizards' magic. The second wave shrugged off their spells like water.
"Now that I have your attention, perhaps I can tell you of the Order."
In the wretched depths of the Grand Coliseum, his soul shines like a single torch blazing in the night.
"Her voice is justice, clear and relentless." —Akroma, angelic avenger
Their grieving faces tell far more than a list of casualties ever could.
Pathmages can open doors that aren't even there.
Some spies seek clarity. Others seek transparency.
"Her voice is insight, piercing and true." —Ixidor, reality sculptor
Many wizards came to the Riptide Project hoping to return home with answers. Most, however, wouldn't return home at all.
The Mirari flares in his mind.
"I have no need of a map. The very continent itself guides my way."
"You cannot fight the storm."
To scrape out a living in Aphetto, wizards are reduced to selling rumors, lies, forgeries, or—if they get desperate enough—the truth.
Taking the form of a junior researcher, the first sliver slipped out of Riptide.
It may wear your face, but its mind is its own.
Though a completely artificial species, primocs are a natural fit for the skies of Otaria.
Those who lead others to wisdom become the wisest themselves.
It wants you to be its chum.
Once the last few slivers the Riptide Project controlled were dead, there was nothing to keep the island from being completely overrun.
"Species XR17 feeds upon the mental energies of its victims. This explains why the goblins remain unaffected." —Riptide Project researcher
New insights yield new senses.
"Their blood is the nectar that nourishes the Cabal." —Phage the Untouchable
"Death couldn't contain the slivers. What made us think we could?" —Riptide Project researcher
Cabal clerics serve two masters: their patriarch and their god.
Death is a secret he is willing to share.
It strikes at your soul, heedless of your prayers.
It oozes death from every pore.
"A single dedicated mind can bring about the greatest destruction. That, or goblins—goblins work too."
"Goblins won't betray their own kind for any price. They'll do it for a very specific price." —Phage the Untouchable
"Her voice is damnation, unyielding and certain." —Phage the Untouchable
A cry of pain as it enters this world. A chorus of screams as it leaves.
Plague and death wrapped in one convenient package.
The Mirari festers in its flesh.
They pick at the remains of the city's corpse.
"Sure, I've seen agents of the Cabal here and there. Well, not here, and certainly not in any of the sliver labs. Oh dear, I've said too much." —Apprentice researcher
It doesn't need to use its venom—it just needs you to know it can.
"The Cabal and the Order really aren't that different. After all, we are both empowered by faith."
Once it consecrated the dead. Now it desecrates them.
Measure its determination by the screams of its prey.
After breaking free from the Riptide Project, the slivers quickly adapted to life on Otaria—much to the dismay of life on Otaria.
The least popular goblins get the outer caves.
"Craghorns experience a wide range of emotions: rage, fury, anger . . ." —Foothill guide
The Mirari burns in his heart.
"How do you stop a raptor from charging? No, seriously! Help!" —Blarg, goblin jester
The more victims he kills, the more likely he is to get the right one.
"Did you know that wood burns even better than rocks?" —Toggo, goblin weaponsmith
Most goblins leave behind a wake of destruction. A few goblins take one with them.
Giant-sized body. Goblin-sized brain.
Daru soldiers learned it's better to have a clean death from a sharp blade than to tangle with a goblin's rusted chains.
"Throw rocks at 'em! Throw spears at 'em! Throw Furt at 'em!"
Once they get the scent, there is no escape.
"Her voice is disaster, painful and final." —Matoc, lavamancer
The goblins tracked the hystrodon with much stealth and cunning. Then they were eaten with much pain and yelling.
As malleable as molten steel, but as dangerous as the finished blade.
"The Skirk Ridge has many wonderful things to discover—like escape routes." —Foothill guide
"I treat each day as your last."
"I order you to volunteer."
Once the goblins thought about it, they preferred being atop a slateback to being in front of, behind, or underneath one.
"The harder we press forward, the harder Krosa pushes us back." —Aven scout
Lorians treat trees and prey the same way: by ripping them limb from limb.
Lucky victims get run over. Unlucky victims get run through.
Within weeks, more slivers nested in Otaria than ever existed on Rath.
"I lost one home when Yavimaya was destroyed. I will not lose another."
Mutated elves wondered if this was their final form, or if it was just another step.
Its diet consists of fruits, plants, small woodland animals, large woodland animals, woodlands, fruit groves, fruit farmers, and small cities.
A herd of one.
"New links are being added to the food chain on a daily basis." —Riptide Project researcher
The first aven scout squad returned from Krosa with disturbing stories. The second returned with disturbing casualties.
The directors of the Riptide Project wanted instant results on the sliver experiments. They got their wish.
"It would take another apocalypse to stop the slivers now." —Riptide Project researcher
"Her voice is wilderness, savage and pure." —Kamahl, druid acolyte
The Mirari pulses in his veins.
Even through the Mirari's voice, the elves still hear the call of their kinship.
"Elves and beasts are tied together, and I am the knot that binds them."
As the Mirari's mutating effects grew out of control, centaurs and druids fled—but insects swarmed closer.
"Your words are meaningless. The rustling of leaves is the only language that makes any sense."
"Most insects have been drawn to the Mirari. But all that remain in Wirewood are under my care."
